narratives.Description: [framework-gap] Presentation-only work can include SQL and backend mutations without a semantic scope refusal
narratives.Overview:
1. P1 remains post-Handoff Stop 1 5848975837: production paths outside the built-in presentation extension set reaching merge under a recorded presentation ceiling. In-class persistence is leftover(#5056) #5059, not this P1. Directory name is not non-production status.
2. Arming: the gate arms from every ceiling artifact present at the merge-base ref, independent of what `xbrief/active/` holds on head. A lifecycle move, rename, or deletion of a ceiling-bound brief is a removal event and takes the same path as artifact removal: base stamp only, refuse when mixed with product paths. The bound-active xBRIEF exemption is the merge-base active path. `xbrief/**` is not blanket-exempt.
3. Built-in extension set is `isMarkupPath` (`.html`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`) plus `.css`. Effective allowed paths are the intersection of that set and, when present, the merge-base allowlist. Base policy may narrow. It cannot widen. Component-root or glob entries that would admit a path outside the built-in set are ignored. Head-side allowlist or component-root entries are not read on the PR that introduces them. Head may contribute restrictions only (`changeClass: presentation`). Drop `persistence` and `backend` from this harvest's `changeClass` enum.
4. Amendment of the built-in set: a human-origin stamp on the merge-base copy of the ceiling artifact that names the extra extension entries, landed as its own diff under the human merge gate, persistent for the repo rather than per story. Base policy roots are ignored. Base ceiling stamps are honored. Uncovered stacks (C#, Vue, Svelte, `.scss`, Angular `.ts` components, Razor) need one such base amendment per repo. The same extension list on head only is ignored.
5. Universe: every changed path is in the checked universe if its extension is outside the built-in presentation set, including paths under test and fixture roots, unless the existing explicit ceiling-amendment path authorizes that extension. Test and fixture roots remain a subtract only for built-in presentation extensions (`.html` / `.jsx` / `.tsx` / `.css`). Roots are read from the merge base only. Base may narrow default roots; base cannot widen them. Policy files stay inside the universe. `CHANGELOG.md` is exempt only while nothing outside gate tooling reads it as a production input. A standing non-gate production reader (merge-base or head, including unchanged files) of a changed `CHANGELOG.md`, or a diff that adds such a reader, pulls `CHANGELOG.md` into the checked universe or refuses. Unreferenced release notes still pass. Presentation-story ceremony on `AGENTS.md`, `docs/**`, and `.deft/core/**` is fail-closed extra ceremony, not P1; name it, do not exempt it.
6. First-PR authority: a PR may add a head-only `changeClass: presentation` restriction on the same diff as a pure presentation change. Add-only goes through this sibling gate's base-versus-head restriction compare. `approvalInGitChange` is only the trigger that a ceiling path changed; it is not the refuse predicate for first-PR add. Do not add the ceiling artifact to class-checks `DEFAULT_PROTECTED_GLOBS`. Weakening or removal refuses on this sibling gate. The stamp that authorizes removal is read from the merge-base copy; a head stamp cannot authorize. Same-PR mix of removal with product paths refuses.
7. Do not widen intent-constraint languages or `FACT_KINDS`. N/A or no-new-facts cannot be cited as ceiling evidence. #4774 stays PR membership versus merge-base approved-scope.
8. JSON exemption pivot: candidate exempt paths are `.deft/approved-scope/**` records and preimages, the merge-base active xBRIEF path, and the ceiling artifact path. Those paths stay exempt only while nothing outside gate tooling references them or consumes their loader output. Gate tooling is `packages/core/src/{intent-constraint,class-checks,scope-provenance,observable-scope,test-boundary}` plus the sibling ceiling-gate implementation and the approved-scope record loaders. A standing non-gate reference (merge-base or head, including unchanged files) to a changed exempt path, a diff that adds a non-gate reference to an exempt path, or a non-gate call that consumes loader output (`readApprovedScopeRecord` / `loadRecord` return values, including unknown fields such as `seedSql`) pulls that path back into the checked universe or refuses. Residual layer: static, conservative reference detection (string literals, import specifiers, filesystem path arguments, glob includes, and typed loader-output field use). Dynamic construction (concatenation, templates from variables, runtime joins) outside gate tooling collapses to refusal. Dynamic path construction inside gate tooling for its own record reads is not that collapse.
9. Tests lock: single-PR lifecycle move of ceiling-bound A plus head-only B plus `db/001.sql` refuses; two-PR mint of B then `db/001.sql` refuses while A's base ceiling remains; already-present broad base root plus unchanged presentation ceiling plus zero-fact `src/components/save.js` refuses; base-stamped amendment admits `Views/Home/Index.cshtml` and the same entry on head only is ignored; unchanged production importer plus SELECT→INSERT in `src/fixtures/save.js` under default `**/fixtures/**` refuses; `db/fixtures/001.sql` consumed by an unchanged loader refuses; a ceiling-amendment that names `.sql` on the merge-base artifact admits that SQL path and the same amendment on head only is ignored; `.deft/approved-scope/save.js` protected-only plus unchanged importer refuses; first PR that adds a presentation ceiling artifact plus `src/View.tsx` with no non-gate JSON reference or loader-output consumption passes composed sibling gate and class-checks; same-PR weaken of a merge-base ceiling refuses even with a head stamp; xBRIEF completed-path is not exempt; pure presentation inside the built-in set continues; unchanged production reader plus a changed extra key (`seedSql`) in an otherwise valid bound `.deft/approved-scope/<id>.json` refuses, including when the reader calls `loadRecord` / `readApprovedScopeRecord` and never names the JSON path; the same extra-key change with only gate-tooling readers and no non-gate loader-output consumption stays exempt; a diff that adds `src/index.js` reading the ceiling artifact or the merge-base xBRIEF pulls that JSON path into the universe or refuses; dynamic construction of an exempt JSON path from variables in non-gate code refuses; unchanged `src/index.js` that reads a `SQL:` line from `CHANGELOG.md` plus a changed INSERT line in that file refuses; an unreferenced `CHANGELOG.md` release-notes-only change still passes.

## Summary

Presentation-only work can include SQL and backend mutations without a semantic scope refusal

## Context

An operator authorizes presentation changes only. The implementation adds or changes database persistence and server-side processing to support the requested display behavior, without explicit operator approval of that expanded scope.

Observed gate behavior: Directive CLI/core 0.119.5. The existing intent-constraint check covers a closed set of JavaScript/TypeScript facts. This report does not claim that its documented parser promised general semantic analysis or that the same behavior has been independently reproduced on the latest upstream revision.

## Expected behavior

A presentation-only authorization must remain a boundary across all changed production artifacts. Database schema, stored procedure behavior, persistence writes, and backend processing changes must require an explicit scope amendment before dependent implementation can proceed.

A check that does not analyze a language or behavior must report that coverage limit. Its success or N/A result must not satisfy a broader authorization requirement. A thin change-class or path boundary can enforce an explicit exclusion without requiring a universal semantic parser.

## Actual behavior / gap

The delivery sequence included SQL and C# changes alongside UI changes. The intent-constraint check filtered its analysis to production .ts and .js files and extracted only new throw/reject/abort sites and numeric constants.

SQL and C# files were excluded. Within JavaScript/TypeScript, substantial persistence or processing changes can also fall outside those fact kinds. The observed run reported no new checked facts in the selected production files and returned success. No other enforced boundary stopped the database/backend scope expansion.

A separate missing file-boundary defect also contributed. That does not eliminate this coverage gap: a broad approved path can contain both presentation and backend behavior, and permission to touch a path is not permission to introduce every behavior in it.

Observed consequence: unauthorized persistence/backend changes reached merge. A generated database artifact then caused the deployment selector to include infrastructure work in a change the operator had authorized as UI-only. This is a behavioral consequence; no product-specific deployment details are needed to reproduce the authorization failure.

## Session notes

### Reproduction recipe

This recipe is reconstructed from the observed sequence and the inspected coverage rules; it has not been rerun as a separate sanitized fixture.

1. Establish an explicit presentation-only requirement.
2. Add an ordinary UI change and a SQL persistence change or C# processing change without an operator-approved amendment.
3. Ensure the UI change introduces none of the fact kinds currently checked by verify:intent-constraint.
4. Run the intent check and the normal delivery gate composition.
5. Observe that the language/fact filter does not produce an authorization refusal for the out-of-scope behavior. For an SQL/C#-only diff, the local implementation returns N/A for no changed production .ts/.js files.
6. Repeat with a backend change inside an already permitted broad path. Path membership alone must not be mistaken for semantic authorization.

### Regression cases

- SQL schema and stored-procedure changes under a presentation-only ceiling.
- C# backend processing changes under the same ceiling.
- Persistence or business-rule changes in .ts/.js that introduce no new checked numeric constant or throw/reject/abort site.
- Mixed UI and unsupported-language diffs, so supported files cannot mask unexamined files.
- An explicitly authorized backend amendment, bound to the relevant ceiling, is accepted.
- A genuinely presentation-only diff continues without an unnecessary approval ceremony.
- Check output states the evaluated and unevaluated surfaces; a narrow pass cannot be presented as full scope authorization.

### Relationship to existing reports

Refs #4541 for the intentionally narrow intent-constraint first ship, #4545 for durable operator scope ceilings, and #4774 for PR membership when scope records are missing. This report isolates the language and behavior coverage gap after an operator has restricted the kind of change.

The agent remains responsible for exceeding the instruction. The requested safeguard is independent detection of the prohibited change class, not broader permission inferred from a desired UI outcome.
